study type: Cross-sectional study with an embedded case-control study
exposure: Maternal fever within 7 days before birth
cohort: The study population comprised all women admitted to three tertiary referral hospitals in southern Ghana with pregnancy-related complications or for birth.
finding: For every maternal death, there were nearly five maternal near-misses, with pre-eclampsia/eclampsia being the leading cause, and women experiencing fever in the 7 days before delivery being six times more likely to have a near-miss.
mod_finding: Spontaneous onset of labour was found to be protective against maternal near-miss.
cross-section timing: Data was collected at the time of admission for pregnancy-related complications or birth, and retrospectively for events within 7 days before birth.
